title: Chapter 49: Xiao Chen, Are You Hurt!
html:
Zhang Peng burst from the workers’ passage and ran blindly through the first floor. The confusing layout and lack of lighting worked against him; within minutes, he had no idea which direction led outside.

“Stop running!” Chen Ge called from behind. “The police are outside. You are only making this harder on yourself.”

“You expect me to trust you after this?” Zhang Peng shouted back. Hurt, frightened, and disoriented, he kept taking whichever corridor looked open.

Chen Ge did not close the distance. “Then trust the police. Just stop before you get yourself hurt in here.”

“You are the least reassuring person I have ever met!” Zhang Peng shouted, disappearing around another turn.

Chen Ge continued after him. Then the scraping sound returned, and a black shadow flashed out from the workers’ passage.

The mirror entity had apparently recognized the opportunity. Zhang Peng rounded a corner and glimpsed a human figure beckoning from farther down the corridor. Terrified of the costumed figure behind him, he ran toward the stranger without thinking.

Chen Ge saw the silhouette and felt a chill run through him. Its build matched the shape that had imitated He Feng. The mirror entity had returned.

“Wrong way! That is not a person!” Chen Ge shouted, but Zhang Peng was already following the figure toward the bathroom.

The first-floor bathroom still has intact mirrors. If it is leading him there, it is about to try something.

The situation was slipping out of control. Chen Ge hurried to the bathroom, only to find the door locked from inside.

This was not how he wanted events to unfold. The shadow had reached Zhang Peng before either Chen Ge or the police could detain him.

“Ahhh!”

A scream burst from behind the door, followed by the crash of something overturning. Whatever Zhang Peng had encountered, it had terrified him.

“What is happening in there?” Chen Ge tried the door, but something heavy had been pushed against it from inside. Unable to see into the room, he shouted for Zhang Peng to move away from the entrance while he searched for another way through.

Bang! Bang! Bang!

The commotion was loud enough to carry outside the Haunted House. After repeated effort, the obstruction shifted just enough to leave a narrow gap.

Through it, Chen Ge saw that the cloth normally covering the mirror had fallen. Zhang Peng stood motionless before the glass—and a large black shadow loomed between him and his reflection.

The shadow slowly changed shape until its outline nearly matched Zhang Peng’s. Then it stepped backward, half of its body seeming to melt into the mirror.

Zhang Peng, still dazed, moved toward the glass as if pulled by an invisible thread. His reflection and the shadow overlapped. A few seconds later, an unnatural smile spread across his otherwise blank face.

He turned slowly and met Chen Ge’s gaze through the gap. Then, with one trembling finger, he traced a symbol across the fogged surface of the mirror.

A moment later, awareness seemed to return to Zhang Peng’s eyes. He shuddered, found the bathroom window, and fled the Haunted House before Chen Ge could reach him.

Did the mirror entity enter Zhang Peng? Is that why it has been so determined to get at me—because I interrupted it before?

The entity had targeted both He San and He Feng, only to be interrupted each time. If it was capable of resentment, Chen Ge had given it more than enough reason to hate the owner of the Haunted House.

The bathroom door was still blocked, so reaching the window from inside would take time. Chen Ge turned toward the front entrance just as Inspector Lee’s voice echoed through the Haunted House.

“Chen Ge! Are you all right? We’re coming in!” A moment later, officers entered the building. Chen Ge immediately stepped away from the costumed props and raised his hands so there could be no misunderstanding.

Footsteps filled the corridor. Inspector Lee was the first to reach him. “Xiao Chen, are you hurt?”

“Shaken, but fine.” Chen Ge pointed toward the bathroom. “Zhang Peng escaped through a window. He cannot have gone far.”

“All right. Leave the rest to us.”

“Gladly.” For once, Chen Ge had no desire to argue.

“And next time, do not put yourself in the middle of something this dangerous.” Inspector Lee sent officers after Zhang Peng while he remained with Chen Ge to examine the Haunted House.

The staff break room was their first stop. Inspector Lee saw the stains and immediately turned. “Xiao Chen, are you sure you are not hurt?”

“That is not mine. I think Zhang Peng injured himself while searching the room in the dark.”

Inspector Lee put on gloves and examined the disturbed bedding and other marks in the room. His expression darkened. “Whatever happened here, he clearly entered with violent intent.”

The scene contained more than enough evidence to support the officers’ concerns about Zhang Peng’s purpose in coming to the Haunted House.

Seeing the room through the police officer’s eyes sent a delayed chill through Chen Ge.

“Do not touch anything in here,” Inspector Lee said. “The evidence team will photograph and process the room.”

“Understood. I’ll cooperate fully.”

Chen Ge left the room and returned to the first-floor bathroom. Standing before the damaged entrance, he remembered one final detail from the encounter.Zhang Peng wrote something on the mirror.
